value.rationale: A separately meaningful 2026 question asks when compact weighted compositions are Hilbert–Schmidt on radial power Fock spaces. The theorem gives explicit counterexamples simultaneously at sub-Gaussian m=1 and all faster integer powers m>=3, with exact transition and logarithmic/power residues. The invariant explains a structural cancellation: angular concentration contributes r^{-m/2} while the radial kernel contributes r^{m-2}, leaving a universal quarter threshold. These constants quantify the severity of non-Hilbert–Schmidt compactness and can benchmark further Schatten or approximation analyses. No claim of solving all m>0 is made.
